name: Universal Boundary Primitive Capacity
description: States true verdicts are not functions of cheap observations. No payload-monotone measure orients the step and message cardinality does not exceed key cardinality.

program.name: The Observation Boundary
program.summary: An observer sends states to records, and its boundary is the set of merged pairs: two distinct states with one record, told apart by no record-determined reading, at infinite resolution cost, repaired by one side symbol whose least alphabet is the largest fiber. The license criterion, under which a target is determined exactly when it is constant on the fibers, is proved on arbitrary sets with its lattice, its Bayes-risk and Blackwell comparison, its Beth gap, the echo law and Shannon's secrecy bound.

oneLine: True verdicts are not functions of cheap observations.
summary: The theory studies typed boundaries where two states share a cheap observation but require different true verdicts, asking when observations orient, certify or license verdicts. It defines the TypedBoundary primitive and its mismatch carrier, together with ciphers, protocols, codes, gradual terms and cost observers. It proves the universal law that no observation-only function returns the true verdict on all states, with instances for mass, provenance, machine confidence, secrecy, agreement, compression and timing. It proves a premise-free pump barrier that any measure with an unbounded payload section at some counter does not orient the duplicating step, including a non-monotone example. It proves a support-level Shannon bound that any perfectly secret cipher on nonempty finite types has message cardinality at most key cardinality, attested by the one-time pad. Classical capacity and impossibility instances for Hamming and syndrome packing, sorting transcripts, Byzantine agreement, partitions, two generals, gradual casts and timing fibers instantiate the same collision, with licensed extensions where an added key, tag, escape summand or healed run restores licensing.
boundary: On one side a cheap observation collides on two states while the true verdict differs, so no function of that observation alone returns the verdict and an added licensing channel is needed. The obstruction is the colliding pair with equal observations and unequal verdicts, which blocks observation-only rules, orientation by a measure with an unbounded section, ciphertext-only licensing under perfect secrecy, and joint availability-consistency and agreement-validity-silence requirements. The universal verdict-not-function theorem locates this limit, and the Shannon message-at-most-key bound with Hamming, syndrome, compression, sorting, Byzantine, partition, gradual, timing and two-generals collisions instantiate it.

conclusions.statement: For every boundary B, there is no function f from B.Obs to B.Verdict such that for all states s, B.verdict s equals f applied to B.observe s.
For every measure m from Nat to Nat to Nat and every counter c, if for every N there exists p with N at most m c p, then m does not orient the duplicating step.

For nonempty finite key and message types with decidable equality on ciphertext and message types, for every cipher E with support-level perfect secrecy, the cardinality of the message type is at most the cardinality of the key type.
Assuming a binary code C corrects t errors, the number of codewords times the radius-t ball cardinality is at most 2 to the power n.
Assuming a parity-check matrix H corrects radius-t errors by syndrome, the radius-t ball cardinality is at most 2 to the power r.
For every n with 0 less than n, the type of shrinking compressors at length n is empty.
For every algorithm A with k comparisons, if 2 to the power k is less than the factorial of the cardinality of Fin n, then it is not the case that A sorts.
For every decision function d from views to Bool, it is not the case that IC1 d and IC2 d both hold.
Assuming the new value differs from the old value, for every responder, it is not the case that the responder is both available on every history and consistent on every partitioned run.
For every protocol P, agreement, validity and no-information-no-attack do not jointly hold.
For every fuel f and bounds m and n, if m differs from n and both costs c m and c n are at most f, then the timing observer does not factor through the output observer.
Safety does not factor through the static type observer infer alone.
The even-payload measure does not orient the duplicating step and is not payload-monotone.
A matrix H corrects radius-t errors by syndrome exactly when its syndrome is injective on the radius-t ball.
Support-level perfect secrecy does not hold for the identity cipher, since ciphertext false reachable from message false is unreachable from message true.

openPoints: Payload monotonicity is recorded as unused; the barrier needs an unbounded payload section at some counter and also blocks an explicit non-monotone even-payload measure, while measures bounded at every counter are not ruled out.
The message-at-most-key bound needs nonempty finite key and message types with decidable equality on ciphertext and message types; the probabilistic Shannon theorem is cited and never re-derived.
The identity cipher fails support-level perfect secrecy, with ciphertext false from message false unreachable from message true, although its ciphertext already licenses the message.
Meeting the sorting count is not shown sufficient; the factorial at three keys is six, two comparisons are insufficient, three meet the count, and an explicit two-comparison algorithm does not sort.

Lossless compression returns with an escape summand or a restricted two-word input; the length-two compressor is empty with count 3 less than 4, and the 1 less than n hypothesis in the boundary construction is recorded as non-load-bearing.
Static-plus-tag licensing holds on well-typed terms with safe subterms; cast-free well-typed terms are safe; the local tag match is recorded for cast safety.

The length-three repetition code attains the Hamming packing bound at radius one and fails correction at radius two via an explicit received collision; the Hamming 7-4 matrix corrects one error with perfect count eight equals eight, while a matrix with two equal columns collides and fails one-error correction.

IC2 alone is satisfiable by returning the received value, while the first-projection rule fails IC1; healed runs license the latest value on unpartitioned runs, and a refusing responder is consistent when it answers but not available.

Timing fibers contain arbitrarily large finite sets with distinct costs, with a two-versus-five collision at fuel 200; numerals alone are constant-time and licensed; each proper subset of two-generals requirements is satisfiable by exhibited protocols.
paperReferences: OB Thm 4.9 `thm:grammar-closure-barrier`; submission Section 6.8; ledger row 01-009
Shannon, "Communication theory of secrecy systems", Bell System Technical Journal 28, 1949

files.summary: This file defines the TypedMismatch carrier with payload, control, verdict and license types and the TypedBoundary primitive of two states with equal cheap observations but different true verdicts, and proves the universal boundary law that the verdict is not a function of the observation. It defines a projection from any boundary to its mismatch carrier with license Unit. It constructs three facet instances, the duplicating-recursor mass boundary, the provenance-versus-license boundary and the machine confidence-versus-certificate boundary, and proves that all three obey the universal law.
files.conclusion: For every typed boundary the true verdict is not a function of the cheap observation.

files.summary: This file defines a three-node one-traitor Byzantine model with Bool values, lieutenant views, loyalty and IC1/IC2 requirements. It constructs three explicit scenarios sA, sB, sC with pairwise view equalities across different required decisions. It proves no symmetric one-round decision function satisfies IC1 and IC2 together, by chaining and by 16-table decide, and packages the sA/sB collision as a universal typed boundary. It also shows IC2 alone is satisfiable while the first-projection rule fails IC1 at sB.
files.conclusion: No symmetric one-relay decision function satisfies both IC1 and IC2 on the three-node one-traitor model.

files.summary: This file defines a reduced two-replica CAP model with wrote and partitioned flags, history and latest-value maps, and availability and consistency predicates. It proves the two partitioned runs collide on empty history with different latest values when values differ, so no responder is both available and consistent there. It proves a healed-partition license plus total responder on unpartitioned runs and a refusing responder that is consistent when it answers but not available. It packages the Boolean collision as a universal typed boundary.
files.conclusion: No responder is both available on every history and consistent on every partitioned run when the new and old values differ.

files.summary: This module defines fixed-length Boolean words and strictly shorter outputs with cardinalities 2^n and 2^n-1, plus a lossless compressor structure. It proves every shorter-output map collides and no positive-length lossless shrinking compressor exists, via fiber-capacity counting, and packages collisions as a universal typed boundary. It also exhibits a lossless escape encoding into a larger sum and a lossless injective encoding of an explicit two-word restriction, with the n=2 count 3<4 and no compressor at n=2.
files.conclusion: For positive n no lossless encoder maps every length-n Boolean word to a strictly shorter word.

files.summary: This file defines a small gradual calculus with nat bool dyn types, static typing, inference, evaluation with cast failure, and safety. It proves inference sound and complete and exhibits good and bad terms sharing static type nat but differing on safety. It proves static types do not license safety, packages that collision as a universal boundary, proves a cast succeeds exactly when its local tag matches, proves the augmented static-plus-tag observer licenses safety on well-typed terms with safe subterms, and proves cast-free well-typed terms are safe.
files.conclusion: Static inference alone does not determine cast safety, but the static type plus local tag does on the retained set and cast-free well-typed terms never fail.

files.summary: This file states a carrier-level pump barrier with no grammar syntax: any Nat to Nat to Nat measure with an unbounded payload section at one counter fails to orient the duplicating step. It derives payload-monotone and grammar-measure forms, noting monotonicity is unused. It defines an even-payload measure that is not monotone but has an unbounded section, so the premise-free barrier blocks it.
files.conclusion: Every measure with an unbounded payload section at some counter does not orient the duplicating step, including a non-monotone example.

files.summary: This file formalizes the binary Hamming sphere-packing bound as a fiber-capacity instance with received word as observer and codeword-error pair as state. It proves minimum distance implies correction, joint-observer licensing, state counting, and the packing product C.card times ball card at most 2^n. It exhibits the length-3 repetition code correcting one error, attaining the bound, and failing at radius two via an explicit received collision packaged as a typed boundary.
files.conclusion: Every binary code correcting t errors satisfies the Hamming packing product bound, attained by rep3 at radius one and violated as correction at radius two.

files.summary: This file defines ciphers with encryption, decryption and correctness, support-level perfect secrecy in which every ciphertext reachable from one message is reachable from every message, and the ciphertext observer, message verdict and key channel on key-message pairs. It proves that the joint ciphertext-key observer licenses the message by decryption, that perfect secrecy yields colliding states with distinct messages so the ciphertext alone does not license the message, and that on finite types the ciphertext fiber holds every message, giving fiber multiplicity at least the message cardinality and hence the support-level Shannon bound through the fiber-capacity law. Shannon's probabilistic theorem is cited and never re-derived. It instantiates the bound with the binary one-time pad, which is perfectly secret with fiber multiplicity two and yields a typed boundary obeying the universal law, and contrasts the identity cipher, which fails perfect secrecy although its ciphertext already licenses the message.
files.conclusion: Any support-level perfectly secret cipher on nonempty finite types satisfies that message cardinality does not exceed key cardinality, with the one-time pad attaining perfect secrecy and the identity cipher failing it.

files.summary: This file defines non-adaptive comparison algorithms with Boolean transcripts and correctness as licensing the sorting permutation. It proves sorting transcripts need at least n factorial capacity, so short transcripts collide and cannot sort, and packages collisions as a universal typed boundary. It computes the n=3 factorial as six, shows two comparisons are insufficient and three meet the count without claiming sufficiency, and exhibits a concrete two-comparison algorithm that does not sort.
files.conclusion: Every fixed non-adaptive k-comparison algorithm with 2^k below n factorial cannot sort all permutations.

files.summary: This file defines binary error vectors, radius-t balls, syndromes, bounded error states, and syndrome correction as licensing. It proves correction is equivalent to syndrome injectivity and implies the syndrome bound ball card at most 2^r via fiber capacity. It proves the Hamming [7,4] matrix corrects one error with a perfect count eight equals eight, and exhibits a colliding matrix Hbad whose two weight-one errors share a syndrome, packaged as a typed boundary that fails one-error correction.
files.conclusion: Syndrome correction of radius-t errors implies the ball-count bound, attained by H74 and refuted for Hbad at radius one.

files.summary: This file defines a System T recursor drain family that always returns zero with step count 3n+1, with fuelled normalization, output and beta-cost observers. It proves exact drain costs, collisions of distinct bounds on output with different costs, non-factorization of timing through output, and a typed boundary at drain 2 versus 5 at fuel 200. It proves timing fibers contain arbitrarily large finite sets with distinct costs and that output licenses cost on numerals alone.
files.conclusion: Functional output does not factor through running time on drain bounds, with unbounded timing fibers and a licensed numeral-only refusal.

files.summary: This file defines alternating views, sender identity, delivery, and finite deterministic protocols with agreement, validity and no-information-no-attack. It proves each sender view is equal with and without its message, so delivery never factors through that view. It proves agreement plus validity forces attack in every run by downward induction, hence no protocol satisfies all three requirements, packages the first rung as a typed boundary, and exhibits protocols satisfying each proper subset of requirements.
files.conclusion: No finite deterministic alternating protocol satisfies agreement, validity, and no-information-no-attack together.

claims.paper: The Orientation Boundary for Step-Duplicating Recursors: A Machine-Checked Structural Theory of Termination Proofs
claims.heading: Thm. 4.9
claims.reason: The bare section theorem gives failure from unboundedness at one counter with no syntax or monotonicity premise, evaluation gives payload-monotonicity of every grammar measure, and counter_orients gives the inhabited escape. Together they cover the barrier claim.
